items.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He was Dizzy’s drummer at that time then Tommy left to go and play with John McLaughlin and Dizzy called me.

ctx.x: Who was it that you replaced? I’m trying to remember.

I replaced a drummer, a young drummer at that time, Tommy Campbell. Great drummer. He was graduated from Berklee. He was Dizzy’s drummer at that time then Tommy left to go and play with John McLaughlin and Dizzy called me. That’s how I got the gig.

Well Ignacio, we’ve been at this for like over an hour, and we have to do like maybe two or three more hours. But I wonder, on a global sense, what do you see as the role and the possibilities of music? You’ve traveled overseas and played for a lot of different populations. Do you have a thought you can share about what you’ve seen music is capable of?
